Pixel art for a small, grimy spaceship cargo bay seen from the side, lit by a few warm lamps against deep shadow. Dark one-pixel outline on characters and props, none on the large hull shapes. Flat colour areas with one highlight pixel and one shadow pixel per surface, light from the upper left, no gradients, no dithering, no anti-aliasing. Muted olive, rust, brown and slate with small bright accents (cheese yellow, lamp orange, screen cyan). Chunky, readable silhouettes with little interior detail: a character is about 14 pixels tall in the game but drawn twice as big (28 to 32 art pixels), a prop 8 to 40.

Draw ONE character: Pip, a small grey mouse astronaut: a round glass space helmet around a grey mouse head with one big pink ear, a stubby orange-and-white spacesuit, short legs with small boots, a long thin pink tail curling behind; walking to the right, full body.

Image 1 is the same character, drawn before: keep its design, proportions, size, colours, outline and its place in the picture exactly, and change only the pose as described below. Image 2 is a POSE GUIDE, not art: coloured lines are the bones of the character in its new pose (the near limbs orange-red, the far limbs blue, the body, neck and head green with the head as a green ring, the tail purple, the yellow line points where the face looks) over a grey silhouette, at the very place and size the character must have. Draw the character of the first image in exactly this pose, there; draw nothing of the guide itself (no lines, dots, grey or white). The reference pictures are shown on a dark grey ground that is not part of the art. Match their pixel size, outline, shading and colours exactly, but draw the new subject: never copy what they show.

Draw it on a pixel grid of exactly 28 x 32 squares: the whole subject is only 28 squares wide and 32 squares tall, so every square is a big flat block of one colour (no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering) and the shape must stay simple and readable at that size. Thin parts such as legs, arms and tails are at least two squares wide. The dark outline is one square wide and runs round the whole silhouette only, not between the parts of the body.
